label: prop:reeb-coefficient-is-hbar-q
title: The Reeb coefficient of $D_\nabla$ is the quantum Planck constant: $1 - q^{-1} = (q-1)/q$
html:
The categorical Dirac operator splits its action into a gradient part and a contact part,

  D_\nabla \;=\; q^{-1}\,\nabla \;+\; \bigl(1 - q^{-1}\bigr)\,\iota_\xi \nabla ,

and its Reeb coefficient is the quantum Planck constant:

  \boxed{\;\; 1 - q^{-1} \;=\; \frac{q-1}{q} \;=\; \hbar_q. \;\;}

The identity is immediate --- both sides clear to q - 1 over q --- and that is the point. Two quantities introduced for unrelated reasons turn out to be one quantity. The coefficient of \iota_\xi\nabla was fixed by demanding that the Dirac operator weight the Reeb direction consistently with the q-connection; the quantum Planck constant was defined as the deformation gap (q-1)/q that measures how far the substrate sits from the classical point q = 1. Neither definition mentions the other.

What the identification says

The quantum Planck constant is a weight, not a length. It is the share of a single application of D_\nabla that flows along the Reeb direction, and the complementary share q^{-1} flows along the gradient. The two are a convex pair, q^{-1} + (1 - q^{-1}) = 1, so the operator is a genuine mixture of the two directions at every q strictly between the classical and Big Bang limits.

Reading \hbar_q as a step cost rather than as a distance settles the relation to the Planck step. Since t_P = 1/\hbar_q counts Reeb operations per unit of time, the product \hbar_q \cdot t_P is the whole circuit, and the two symbols measure a fraction and its reciprocal rather than two competing scales. That reading is made explicit in share versus total; the finite-q consequence for the induced metric is the Reeb-step-count qualification.

Archimedean specialisation. What follows sits on the archimedean side of the substrate wall: it invokes real- or complex-analytic constructs --- real-valued physical observables, real-analytic bounds, transcendental constants, or numerical evaluation at the substrate parameter q_0. Any generic categorical or q-deformation identities it draws on remain valid over an abstract coefficient ring; only their archimedean realisation is specialised here. At q_0 = 1.10997858275138080759 the Reeb share is \hbar_{q_0} = 0.09908171604425850784 and the gradient share is q_0^{-1} = 0.90091828395574149216, with t_P(q_0) = 10.09267945615024539110.
